summary: All in-scope presentation work is implemented, verified against the real built preview, and committed as 1c732dc1 in the ORI-VIS-001 worktree: PageHeader is now the editorial masthead (balanced title, muted one-liner, token hairline); Prose carries the full reading rhythm (70ch measure kept, token-driven links replacing UA blue, quiet lists/blockquotes, anchored headings) and confines command surfaces as single-line pre with their own horizontal scroller in --font-mono; Toc is the Astro-owned <details> control (bordered collapsible block below xl, sticky 14rem rail with its own vertical scroller at >=xl); DocsLayout preloads the latin Spline subsets; global.css gains the four self-hosted @font-face rules (Spline Sans / Spline Sans Mono Variable, latin + latin-ext, font-display swap, same-origin, OFL 1.1 committed under apps/docs/public/fonts, force-added because public/ is gitignored for generated r/ — prebuild only wipes public/r so fonts survive rebuilds) plus one token treatment for the CopyButton trigger so no UA system button face renders in install strips (CodeBlock/CopyButton sources byte-identical to their landed sprint-04 contracts). RED run recorded before implementation (.tmp/ORI-VIS-001/cycle-1/red), final run 9/12 green; the 3 failures are one assertion failing identically in all three projects. Gates: docs build green, pnpm typecheck green, biome ci green on apps/docs/src + the spec. Visual verification done against the real screenshots: pixel-sampled evidence PNGs (light bg 255, dark bg 10, hairline 229 = --border, tab pill 229 = --primary with 63 text, trigger 38 = --secondary with 250 text after the fix, both stacked no-JS panels confirmed by DOM probe) plus computed-style probes. The blocker: AC-2 requires 'Section navigation reaches /docs/installation, /docs/cli, /docs/theming and /docs/dark-mode', but the nav on every docs page derives from sectionNavigation() in apps/docs/src/lib/docs-navigation.ts, whose RESERVED_DOC_SLUGS mechanism excludes the theming slug from the nav entirely (its own comment says the static route owns the destination 'until ORI-AST-003 adapts it' — AST-003 landed but never adapted the nav). Observed nav hrefs: introduction, installation, quickstart, cli, dark-mode, owns-vs-does-not-own — no theming, so the Guides section group is absent everywhere. Fixing it means editing apps/docs/src/lib/docs-navigation.ts, which is outside this task's exact write allowlist and in the write-prohibited 'Routing' class. The fix itself is one semantic line: let sectionNavigation include the reserved theming entry (under its 'guides' section) while the catch-all keeps excluding it from route generation; no landed test asserts theming's absence from nav. I did not weaken the assertion — it fails loudly in all three projects as the recorded evidence of the mismatch.
assumptions: Toc renders as <details open>: open-by-default at every width (static HTML cannot vary the open attribute per viewport without JS), user-togglable everywhere, chevron affordance below xl, restyled as the sticky rail at >=xl; the summary stays a live toggle at rail width so a collapsed rail can always reopen.

boundary-table.png is the boundary page evidence exactly as authored: ORI-CONT-005's manuscript contains no table (ownership split is prose + lists), and the task notes the filename is an evidence path, not authorization to expand into the Sprint 06 boundary-table use case — no table was fabricated.

Command confinement is scoped to .prose: .copy-button__command becomes white-space:pre + overflow-x:auto + flex shrink so long single-line commands scroll inside their own container instead of wrapping mid-URL; the ledger/home strip treatment is untouched.

The CopyButton trigger token treatment lives in global.css (allowlisted) because sprint-04's contract test pins CopyButton.astro and CodeBlock.astro byte-identical to their landed state; the rule adds no hover gating, only token colors.
No-JS contexts render the dark column by construction (the pre-paint theme flip is an is:inline script), so installation-nojs.png and the no-JS engine-panel proofs are dark-theme observations.

Direct page.request.get checks on woff2 accept 200 or 304 (304 = cache revalidation after the browser's initial 200 load within the same context); the first observed browser response per font URL must be exactly 200.

Font binaries are the foundry variable woff2 subsets (Spline Sans 300-700, Spline Sans Mono 300-700, latin + latin-ext) fetched from Google Fonts' CDN with their SIL OFL 1.1 license text committed alongside.
blockers: AC-2 member 'section navigation reaches /docs/theming' fails in chromium-desktop, chromium-mobile and chromium-nojs: apps/docs/src/lib/docs-navigation.ts RESERVED_DOC_SLUGS excludes theming from sectionNavigation, so no docs page's section nav links /docs/theming. The fix file is outside this task's write allowlist (routing/publication contract, write_prohibited 'Routing'). Either grant a one-line scope addition to docs-navigation.ts (include the reserved slug in the nav derivation while the catch-all keeps excluding it from generation) or reroute the AC-2 member's mechanism; the committed spec already encodes the assertion and fails honestly until then.

scope_impact.found: apps/docs/src/lib/docs-navigation.ts:48 RESERVED_DOC_SLUGS=['theming'] is consumed by both publishedDocs (route generation exclusion, correct — the static /docs/theming route owns the destination) and sectionNavigation (nav derivation), so the reserved slug is silently absent from every page's section nav and the Guides group never renders.
scope_impact.change: Needed: include the reserved theming entry in the sectionNavigation derivation only (one semantic line in docs-navigation.ts, outside this task's allowlist). Everything else in AC-2 — nav reaches installation/cli/dark-mode, TextClassContext heading below the 3.5rem header, 70ch measure, details-based ToC — is green across all three projects.
